posture_reason: only one corner of credit is strained; lenders broadly are calm, yet AMBER alone has historically doubled the odds of a 10% fall and protection is expensive — structures that sell the rich vol fit better than outright puts

Regime: credit-tail — one corner of the credit market is strained (the weakest borrowers, or a single fund or asset class) while lenders broadly stay calm — watch, not yet the serious kind

Protection posture: Protection is dear — spreads or collars rather than outright — only one corner of credit is strained; lenders broadly are calm, yet AMBER alone has historically doubled the odds of a 10% fall and protection is expensive — structures that sell the rich vol fit better than outright puts. (Your own rules, applied mechanically — not advice.)
Cost of protection (not part of the score): Cost of crash insurance — expensive, Cost of insurance overall — expensive, Cost of Nasdaq crash insurance — middling

indicators.label: Junk-bond risk premium
indicators.detail: The extra yield lenders demand to lend to risky companies rather than to the government: 3.31%, +0.20 points over the past week. Lenders are getting nervous above 4.5%, or on a jump of more than 0.30 points in a week. A fast jump is the earliest reliable warning signal here.

indicators.label: Safe-borrower risk premium
indicators.detail: The same measure for financially solid companies: 0.85%. It barely budges in normal times, so any real move means the worry has spread beyond the risky end of the market. Nervous above 1.3%. Both ends calm (risky borrowing costs 3.9× the solid kind, which is normal).

indicators.label: Weakest-borrower risk premium
indicators.detail: The same measure for the shakiest borrowers of all: 12.97%. This is the closest free stand-in for the debt-funded AI buildout, and trouble usually shows up here before anywhere else. Nervous above 10.0%.

indicators.label: Junk bonds vs government bonds
indicators.detail: Are investors dumping risky bonds and buying safe government ones? This is priced continuously through the trading day, so it moves before the official spread figures, which arrive a day late. A fall of 1.5% or more over two weeks is the warning.

indicators.label: Bank loans to risky companies
indicators.detail: These loans pay a floating interest rate, so their price moves on worry about the companies rather than on interest-rate swings — a cleaner read on company health than bonds give you. Moving in step with junk bonds (-0.1 points over two weeks).

indicators.label: Overnight cash squeeze
indicators.detail: What banks pay to borrow cash overnight, against what the Fed pays them to leave it parked. Normally near zero or a little below; currently -2 basis points (a basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point). Staying above +8 means cash is getting scarce in the banking system.

indicators.label: Cash squeeze severity
indicators.detail: Two checks that tell a real cash shortage from the routine month-end and quarter-end noise. First, the gap between what the most desperate borrowers pay and what a typical one pays: 11 basis points, where 30 or more is unusual. Second, the Fed's standing emergency lending window — banks borrowed $0.1 billion on the busiest of the last three days, where $5 billion or more is worth noticing. Ordinary calendar spikes show neither, which is why both have to agree before this counts as stress.

indicators.label: Overall borrowing conditions
indicators.detail: A weekly summary from the Chicago Fed of how easy it is to borrow across the whole economy. Above zero means tighter than the historical average. It moves slowly, so it carries little weight here.

indicators.label: Fear now vs fear later
indicators.detail: Investors normally expect more turbulence three months out than today, which keeps this below 1.00. Above 1.00 the market is pricing the trouble as happening now — a confirmation that something is already underway, worth days of warning at most rather than weeks.

indicators.label: Cost of crash insurance
indicators.detail: How pricey insurance against a big fall is compared with ordinary options: 162, where 145 or more counts as expensive. VVIX 107 measures how pricey it is for that insurance to pay off explosively rather than merely well (expensive above 110). Protection is pricey — you would be paying up for exactly the outcome you want to insure against. This can read expensive in a perfectly calm market: it is about the price of insurance, not the odds of a crash, which is why it is not part of the score.

indicators.label: Cost of insurance overall
indicators.delta: pricier than 69% of the year · Nasdaq
indicators.detail: Priced on the Nasdaq. Two ways to check. The turbulence the market expects is running at 25.6, higher than 69% of the past year (expensive above 80%). And shares have actually been moving about 15.8, so you would be paying +9.8 points for turbulence that has not arrived (expensive above 8). This is a rough market-wide guide — check the price of the specific option before buying. Not part of the score.

indicators.label: Cost of Nasdaq crash insurance
indicators.detail: Read straight off the QQQ option chain (expiry 2026-11-20, 31 days): a put 25% likely to pay costs 25.6% implied volatility against 18.5% for the mirror-image call — +7.1 points more for downside than upside (expensive above 9). Relative to at-the-money (21.5%) that is ×1.19 (expensive above 1.4). Nasdaq downside insurance is middling in price. This is the price of the actual instrument, not an S&P proxy. Not part of the score.

indicators.label: AI stocks vs their recent highs
indicators.detail: An equal-weight basket of 14 AI-exposed companies, currently 12.3% below its three-month high, having moved -11.4% over the past two weeks. Equal-weight means a small company counts as much as a giant one, so a single megacap cannot mask the rest.

indicators.label: Most fragile AI companies
indicators.detail: CoreWeave and Oracle stand for the debt-funded end of the AI buildout. What their own lenders charge them is not published for free, so we watch for sharp share-price falls, or a sudden jump in how much the shares swing day to day, as the stand-in.

indicators.label: Breadth of the market
indicators.detail: When gains narrow to a handful of giant companies the market gets fragile. Two checks: the average US stock against the big-company index (+1.3% over the past month), and how much of the AI basket is still above its 50-day average (21%). A slow background signal, so it carries little weight.

indicators.label: Yield curve
indicators.detail: Long-term government borrowing costs minus short-term. When it goes negative — short-term paying more than long — a downturn has often followed, but 6 to 18 months later, which is no use for timing. Capped so it can never trigger a red on its own.

paper.rules: Fake $1,000 in QQQ from day one. Once per trading day (post-close): cheap-protection window → buy the ~5%-below put, notional-matched; spreads-or-collars → open the 5→15 put spread; trim → sell 25% of shares, once per episode; GREEN → put cash back into QQQ. Options marked at chain mids, settled at intrinsic on expiry. Benchmark: the same shares, never touched.
